nodes.title: Polarized deformation problems
nodes.statement: Let 𝒢_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} with j(g, μ)j^{−1} = (μ·ᵗg^{−1}, μ), and ν : 𝒢_n → GL_1 sending (g, μ) ↦ μ and j ↦ −1. Let r̄ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(k) be continuous with r̄^{−1}((GL_n × GL_1)(k)) = G_{F,S}, and χ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒪^× a lift of ν ∘ r̄. A lift of r̄ to A ∈ C_𝒪 is a continuous r : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(A) reducing to r̄ with ν ∘ r = χ; lifts are equivalent when conjugate by 1 + M_n(𝔪_A); T-framed lifts (r; α_v)_{v∈T} are identified with (βrβ^{−1}; βα_v). A polarized global deformation problem 𝒮 = (F/F⁺, S, S̃, 𝒪, r̄, χ, {D_v}) takes for each v ∈ S a local deformation problem D_v for r̄|G_{F_ṽ} (GL_n-valued, as in R04.3); a lift is of type 𝒮 when each r|G_{F_ṽ} ∈ D_v. Equivalently (Lemma 2.1.1), for γ₀ ∈ G_{F⁺} ∖ G_F, a lift is a triple (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩): ρ = r|G_F, μ = χ, and a perfect pairing with ⟨x, ρ(γ₀²)y⟩ = −μ(γ₀)⟨y, x⟩ and μ(δ)⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨ρ(δ)x, ρ(γ₀δγ₀^{−1})y⟩, i.e. an actual polarization ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ μ.
hypotheses: F/F⁺ is a CM extension (F⁺ totally real, F totally imaginary quadratic over F⁺), S a finite set of finite places of F⁺ that split in F and contain the places above p, S̃ a choice of one place ṽ of F above each v ∈ S, and p odd.
The pairing, multiplier, symmetry sign and oddness sign of polarizations are requested from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7; this node takes them as given.

r̄ is Schur (CHT Definition 2.1.6) when every irreducible G_F-subquotient is absolutely irreducible and no subquotient W₂ satisfies W₂^∨ ⊗ ν∘r̄ ≅ (k^n/W₁)^{γ₀}; r̄|G_F absolutely irreducible suffices.
Fixed-multiplier variant: ν ∘ r = χ is imposed. Coefficient extension along 𝒪 → 𝒪′ is as in R04.1/change-of-coefficients.
proofSteps: Lemma 2.1.1: write r(γ₀) = (A, −μ(γ₀))j and put ⟨x, y⟩ = ᵗxA^{−1}y; the relations in 𝒢_n translate into the two pairing identities, and conversely.
At a complex conjugation c_v (v | ∞), r(c_v) = (A, −χ(c_v))j with ᵗA = −χ(c_v)A, so the pairing is symmetric or alternating according to the sign −χ(c_v) (Lemma 2.1.3's computation).
acceptance: n = 1: 𝒢₁-valued lifts are characters ψ of G_F with ψ^c = ψ^{−1}·χ|G_F, together with the sign data.
The correspondence of Lemma 2.1.1 is a bijection between 𝒢_n-valued homomorphisms (inducing Γ/Δ ≅ 𝒢_n/𝒢_n⁰) and triples (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩).
If r̄|G_F = ψ ⊕ ψ^{c,∨}χ is reducible with the two summands exchanged by the polarization, r̄ is not Schur, and the deformation functor need not be representable.

nodes.statement: If r̄ is Schur, the functor Def^{□_T}_𝒮 of T-framed polarized deformations of type 𝒮 is represented by R^{□_T}_𝒮 ∈ C_𝒪 (R^univ_𝒮 for T = ∅). There is a tautological map R^loc_{𝒮,T} := ⊗̂_{v∈T} R^loc_v/I_v → R^{□_T}_𝒮, and Hom(𝔪/(𝔪², λ, 𝔪_{R^loc}), k) ≅ H¹_{𝒮,T}(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄). A choice of universal lift r^univ_𝒮 gives R^{□_T}_𝒮 ≅ R^univ_𝒮⟦X_{v,i,j} : v ∈ T, 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n⟧, in n²|T| variables.
hypotheses: F/F⁺ is a CM extension (F⁺ totally real, F totally imaginary quadratic over F⁺), S a finite set of finite places of F⁺ that split in F and contain the places above p, S̃ a choice of one place ṽ of F above each v ∈ S, and p odd.
ad r̄ is g_n = M_n(k) with 𝒢_n acting by ad(g, μ)(x) = gxg^{−1} and ad(j)(x) = −ᵗx; over ℤ[1/2], g_n^{𝒢_n} = 0.

Contrast with variable-determinant-representability: there the framing adds n²|T| − 1 variables, because scalars centralise a GL_n-valued lift; here the centraliser of r^univ in 1 + M_n(𝔪) is trivial (CHT Lemma 2.1.11), so no variable is removed.
proofSteps: Lifts of type 𝒮 are representable (properties 1–4 of local deformation problems); passing to equivalence classes is a quotient by the smooth group functor 1 + M_n(𝔪), representable because stabilisers lift (trivially for T ≠ ∅, by Lemma 2.1.11 for T = ∅).

Tangent space: T-framed lifts to k[ε] trivial at T are ((1 + φε)r̄; 1 + a_vε) with φ ∈ Z¹(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄), φ|G_{F_ṽ} = (ad r̄ − 1)a_v on T and φ|G_{F_ṽ} ∈ L¹_v off T, modulo coboundaries: this is H¹ of C•_{𝒮,T}(ad r̄).
Framing: (r^univ_𝒮; 1 + (X_{v,i,j})) is universal, since the centraliser of r^univ_𝒮 in 1 + M_n(𝔪) is {1}.
acceptance: T = ∅: R^univ_𝒮 itself.
|T| = 1: n² framing variables (not n² − 1).
Without the Schur hypothesis the unframed functor can fail to be representable, as for GL_n-valued deformations of reducible representations.

nodes.title: Tangent and obstruction spaces of polarized problems
nodes.statement: For a polarized problem 𝒮 with r̄ Schur and T ⊆ S: obstructions to lifting a T-framed lift of type 𝒮 along a small extension R → R/I lie in H²_{𝒮,T}(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄) ⊗ I (CHT Lemma 2.2.11). Moreover H^i_{𝒮,T} = 0 for i > 3; H⁰_{𝒮,T} = H⁰(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄) if T = ∅ and 0 otherwise; h³_{𝒮,T} = h⁰(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄(1)); h²_{𝒮,T} = h¹_{L^⊥,T}(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄(1)); and χ_{𝒮,T}(ad r̄) = Σ_{v|∞} n(n + χ(c_v))/2 + Σ_{v∈S∖T}(h⁰(G_{F_ṽ}, ad r̄) − dim L_v). When p ∤ n, g_n = g_n⁰ ⊕ k (scalars, on which j acts by −1); when p | n the scalars lie in g_n⁰, there is no such splitting, and one must work with ad r̄ = g_n rather than pass to trace zero.
hypotheses: F/F⁺ is a CM extension (F⁺ totally real, F totally imaginary quadratic over F⁺), S a finite set of finite places of F⁺ that split in F and contain the places above p, S̃ a choice of one place ṽ of F above each v ∈ S, and p odd.

The Euler characteristic over G_{F⁺,S}, where F(S)/F⁺ may ramify outside S (CHT Lemma 2.3.3, valid since p ∤ [F : F⁺] = 2), and Poitou–Tate duality in this setting are requested from ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7; the dual Selmer dimension count in all ranks, including the trace-kernel exceptions for p | n, is D8.
dim g_n^{c=η} = n(n + η·χ(c))/2 for a complex conjugation c (CHT Lemma 2.1.3), which produces the archimedean terms.
proofSteps: Obstruction class: pick set-theoretic lifts of r(γ) and of α_v, form the 2-cochain φ and the local 1-cochains ψ_v; (φ, (ψ_v)) is a 2-cocycle of C•_{𝒮,T} whose class vanishes exactly when a lift of type 𝒮 exists (Lemma 2.2.11).
Vanishing and H⁰, H³, H²: the long exact sequence of C• with H^i(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄) = H^i(G_{F,S}, ad r̄)^{Gal(F/F⁺)}, compared with the Poitou–Tate sequence (Lemma 2.3.4 (1)–(4)).
Euler characteristic: Lemma 2.2.8, the global formula of Lemma 2.3.3, the local Euler characteristic formula (Σ_{v∈S} χ(G_{F_ṽ}, ad r̄) = n²[F⁺ : ℚ]) and Lemma 2.1.3.

If χ(c_v) = −1 for all v | ∞ (the 'odd' sign for CHT's applications), the archimedean term is [F⁺ : ℚ]·n(n − 1)/2.
p = n = 3: the scalar matrix 1 has trace 3 = 0, so k·1 ⊂ g₃⁰ and g₃ ≠ g₃⁰ ⊕ k.

nodes.title: Presentations of polarized deformation rings
nodes.statement: If r̄ is Schur, R^{□_T}_𝒮 is a quotient of a power series ring over R^loc_{𝒮,T} in g = h¹_{L^⊥,T}(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄(1)) + Σ_{v∈S∖T}(dim L_v − h⁰(G_{F_ṽ}, ad r̄)) − h⁰(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄(1)) − Σ_{v|∞} n(n + χ(c_v))/2 variables. If each D_v with v ∈ S ∖ T is liftable, h¹_{L^⊥,T}(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄(1)) relations suffice, so R^□_𝒮 has Krull dimension at least 1 + Σ_{v∈T}(dim R^loc_v/I_v − 1) + Σ_{v∈S∖T}(dim L_v − h⁰(G_{F_ṽ}, ad r̄)) − h⁰(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄(1)) − Σ_{v|∞} n(n + χ(c_v))/2. These statements concern R^{□_T}_𝒮 itself; its p-torsion-free quotient and the reduced ring of its generic fibre are different objects, and component statements used in patching refer to the latter.
hypotheses: F/F⁺ is a CM extension (F⁺ totally real, F totally imaginary quadratic over F⁺), S a finite set of finite places of F⁺ that split in F and contain the places above p, S̃ a choice of one place ṽ of F above each v ∈ S, and p odd.

The rank-n local conditions used in applications (ordinary, bounded-height, Fontaine–Laffaille, with their tangent dimensions dim L_v and liftability, as in CHT Corollary 2.3.6) come from LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7, the supplier RS-08 names for G7; the away-from-p conditions preserving monodromy come from R08.2.
proofSteps: Corollary 2.2.12: a minimal presentation over R^loc_{𝒮,T} has h¹_{𝒮,T} generators and at most h²_{𝒮,T} relations when the local problems off T are liftable.
Substitute Lemma 2.3.4 (polarized-tangent-obstruction) for h¹ and h²: this is Corollary 2.3.5.
If H²_{𝒮,T} = 0 and each D_v off T is liftable, R^{□_T}_𝒮 is a power series ring over R^loc_{𝒮,T} (Corollary 2.2.13).
acceptance: CHT Corollary 2.3.6: if H¹_{L^⊥} = 0, every D_v is liftable, and the L_v have the Fontaine–Laffaille/minimal dimensions, then χ(c_v) = −1 at all v | ∞ and R^univ_𝒮 = 𝒪.
T = S (fully framed): the sum over S ∖ T is empty.
Dimension bounds do not give flatness over 𝒪: R^{□_T}_𝒮 may have p-torsion, so its generic-fibre components must be studied on the p-torsion-free quotient.

nodes.title: Taylor–Wiles places in rank n
nodes.statement: Let v ∤ p with q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|G_{F_v} unramified with n distinct k-rational eigenvalues α_{v,1}, …, α_{v,n} of ρ̄(Frob_v) in a fixed order. Every lift of ρ̄|G_{F_v} to A is GL_n(A)-conjugate to γ₁ ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ γ_n for unique characters γ_i lifting the unramified characters with Frob_v ↦ α_{v,i}. With Δ_v = k(v)^×(p)^n (k(v)^×(p) the maximal p-power quotient), the characters γ_i ∘ Art_{F_v}|𝒪^×_{F_v} give a canonical local 𝒪-algebra map 𝒪[Δ_v] → R^□_v, depending on the ordering, which is formally smooth of relative dimension n². For a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q, (α_{v,i})), the augmented problem 𝒮_Q (unrestricted D^□_v at v ∈ Q) makes R^T_{𝒮_Q} a Λ[Δ_Q]-algebra (Δ_Q = ∏_{v∈Q} Δ_v), and R^T_{𝒮_Q} → R^T_𝒮 has kernel 𝔞_Q R^T_{𝒮_Q}, 𝔞_Q the augmentation ideal.
hypotheses: F is a number field, 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension E/ℚ_p containing the images of all embeddings of F, with residue field k, and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(k) is continuous and absolutely irreducible, with p ∤ 2n (ACC+'s standing hypotheses).

This is the rank-n form of GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 (taylor-wiles-local-cohomology, taylor-wiles-inertia-action), which treats n = 2. ACC+ leave the proof of Lemma 6.2.19 to the reader, citing DDT Lemma 2.44.
proofSteps: Diagonalisation: the tame inertia acts through a pro-p quotient on which ρ(Frob_v) acts with distinct residual eigenvalues; Hensel's lemma splits A^n into Frobenius eigenlines, each stable under inertia since q_v ≡ 1 mod p and the commutation relation σ_v φ_v σ_v^{−1} = φ_v^{q_v}.
The characters restricted to 𝒪^×_{F_v} factor through k(v)^×(p) as they are pro-p; this defines 𝒪[Δ_v] → R^□_v, formally smooth of relative dimension n² (the conjugation parameters).
Augmentation: a lift of type 𝒮_Q is of type 𝒮 exactly when all γ_i are unramified, i.e. when Δ_Q acts trivially.
acceptance: n = 2 recovers R04.5's Taylor–Wiles places.
|k(v)^×(p)| = p^{v_p(q_v − 1)}, so q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N gives |Δ_v| ≥ p^{Nn}.
If ρ̄(Frob_v) has a repeated eigenvalue the splitting into characters fails, and R^□_v is not formally smooth over 𝒪[Δ_v].

nodes.title: Taylor–Wiles primes for enormous image
nodes.statement: Let T ⊆ S, F CM with maximal totally real subfield F⁺, ζ_p ∉ F, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous. Let q ≥ h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)). For every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q_N, (α_{v,i})) with #Q_N = q, q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N and v of degree one over ℚ for each v ∈ Q_N, and h¹_{𝒮_{Q_N}^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) = 0. Here k contains all eigenvalues of ρ̄(G_F), and the choices may avoid any additional finite set of places.
hypotheses: F is a number field, 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension E/ℚ_p containing the images of all embeddings of F, with residue field k, and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(k) is continuous and absolutely irreducible, with p ∤ 2n (ACC+'s standing hypotheses).

Enormous (ACC+ Definition 6.2.28 in arXiv v2): H absolutely irreducible with no nontrivial p-power quotient, H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0, and every simple k[H]-submodule W ⊆ ad⁰ has W^h ≠ 0 for some regular semisimple h ∈ H; independent of k (Lemma 6.2.29). The definition and its invariance are requested from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, which owns residual-image conditions.

p ∤ n is used for ad ρ̄ = k ⊕ ad⁰ρ̄. The shared Chebotarev, finite-avoidance, degree-one and exact-cardinality steps are imported from R04.5/chebotarev-selmer-selection; G7 verifies the enormous-image detecting-element hypotheses and the arbitrary-rank dual Selmer interpretation.

Use ACC+ §6.2.28–Lemma 6.2.32 in the published version (Definition 6.2.28 and Lemma 6.2.31 in arXiv v2). S contains places above p and residual ramification, T ⊆ S, N ≥ 1, and the coefficient field contains all eigenvalues of ρ̄(G_F).
proofSteps: For each nonzero class κ in H¹_{𝒮⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)), verify the detecting-element input to R04.5/chebotarev-selmer-selection: σ in G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}, ρ̄(σ) regular semisimple with k-rational eigenvalues, and p_σ κ(σ) ≠ 0. Use the direct sum ad = k ⊕ ad⁰; a nonzero component gives a nonzero projection of the full class without cancellation between these summands.

ad⁰ part: since H = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) has no p-power quotient, H = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}); H⁰(H, ad⁰) = H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0 make restriction to Gal(F_S/L(ζ_{p^N})) injective, and the regular-semisimple condition gives σ₀; adjust by τ ∈ G_{L(ζ_{p^N})} if needed.
Scalar part: κ ∈ H¹(F_S/F, k(1)) is a Kummer class; as ζ_p ∉ F the Kummer extension is non-abelian over F, hence nontrivial over F(ζ_{p^N}) and disjoint from the field cut out by ρ̄.

Pass to a finite quotient carrying ρ̄, the cyclotomic character and the cocycle. The nonzero projected evaluation is unchanged under cocycle coboundaries and conjugacy, hence gives the required detecting Frobenius class. A regular-semisimple element in the same cyclotomic kernel supplies the admissible padding class. Apply the R04.5 lemma with the forbidden set S and any extra finite set. D8 identifies the localization kernel with the dual Selmer group of 𝒮_Q. Thus #Q = q and the augmented dual Selmer group vanishes without a second prime-selection proof.
acceptance: n = 2 and p ≥ 7: a subgroup of GL₂(k) containing SL₂(𝔽_p) is enormous (SL₂(𝔽_p) is perfect, H⁰ and H¹ of ad⁰ vanish, and diag(a, a^{−1}) with a² ≠ 1 fixes the diagonal of ad⁰), so these primes exist. For p = 5, H¹(SL₂(𝔽₅), ad⁰) ≠ 0.
If ζ_p ∈ F the scalar part fails: Kummer classes can become trivial on G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}, and no such Q_N need exist.
If p | n no subgroup is enormous (the scalars lie in ad⁰), so the lemma is vacuous.

Changing coefficient field to contain residual eigenvalues uses ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 and the coefficient-change interface; it does not silently strengthen a theorem stated over a smaller k.

nodes.statement: Take T = S and q ≥ h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)). Assume F = F⁺F₀ with F⁺ totally real and F₀ imaginary quadratic, ζ_p ∉ F, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous. The auxiliary group Δ_{Q_N} = ∏_{v∈Q_N} k(v)^×(p)^n is a product of qn cyclic p-groups, each of order at least p^N; this is what complex patching receives.
hypotheses: F is a number field, 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension E/ℚ_p containing the images of all embeddings of F, with residue field k, and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(k) is continuous and absolutely irreducible, with p ∤ 2n (ACC+'s standing hypotheses).

ACC+ Proposition 6.2.33 in the published version, verified here at printed p. 1047; Proposition 6.2.32 in arXiv v2. The residual hypothesis is enormous image, not adequacy. k contains all eigenvalues of ρ̄(G_F). T = S contains all p-adic and residual ramification places, and q is at least the stated dual Selmer dimension.
It is stated for G8's variable-determinant problem; RS-08 places it in G7 together with the Taylor–Wiles lemma.
proofSteps: Apply enormous-taylor-wiles-primes using the shared R04.5 selector, additionally excluding places over rational primes ramified in F₀. A degree-one place over an unramified rational prime forces that prime to split in the quadratic F₀. Apply G8/variable-determinant-presentation, published Proposition 6.2.25, to 𝒮_Q with T = S.
g = −h⁰(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) − n²[F⁺ : ℚ] + Σ_{v∈Q_N}(dim L_v − h⁰(F_v, ad ρ̄)): F has [F⁺ : ℚ] complex places, each with h⁰ = n², and h¹_{𝒮_{Q_N}^⊥,T} = 0.

h⁰(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) = 0 by enormousness and ζ_p ∉ F; for v ∈ Q_N, L_v = H¹(F_v, ad ρ̄) and dim L_v − h⁰(F_v, ad ρ̄) = h⁰(F_v, ad ρ̄(1)) = n (local duality, the Euler characteristic, q_v ≡ 1 mod p and distinct eigenvalues).
acceptance: n = 2, F⁺ = ℚ, F = F₀ imaginary quadratic: g = 2q − 4.
With q = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) exactly, the number of variables is determined by the dual Selmer group; a larger q only adds variables and auxiliary primes.
If F does not contain an imaginary quadratic F₀ in the way stated, the split-in-F₀ condition cannot be imposed, and ACC+'s local-global compatibility arguments need it.

The count is a nonnegative integer proved by its identification with a relative tangent dimension, before it is used to index variables. Natural-number subtraction must not silently truncate a negative expression.

PA.4 must receive both the Λ[Δ_Q]-action and the augmentation quotient R^T_{𝒮_Q}/𝔞_Q ≅ R^T_𝒮. The ring presentation does not construct arithmetic complexes or establish their uniform boundedness.

nodes.title: Shared Chebotarev selection for Selmer detection
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, k a finite field, H a finite-dimensional k-space of continuous global cohomology classes, and loc_v : H → H_v the specified linear localization maps at admissible unramified finite places. Assume that every nonzero x in H has a detecting Frobenius conjugacy class in a finite Galois extension of F: every place in that class outside a finite exceptional set is admissible and has loc_v(x) ≠ 0. Assume also a nonempty admissible Frobenius class for padding, including when H = 0. For every finite avoidance set B and integer q ≥ dim_k H, one can choose exactly q distinct admissible places outside B with joint localization H → ∏ H_v injective. The places can all have degree one over Q. Congruence and eigenvalue constraints are preserved when encoded in the finite quotient and its conjugacy-invariant admissibility condition. This is a conditional arithmetic selection lemma, not a residual-image theorem or a new density theorem.
hypotheses: The detecting class, finite quotient and exceptional set may depend on x and on the prescribed level N. Continuity into finite coefficient modules provides finite quotients of the relevant cocycles; the application must prove the detection property is invariant under conjugacy and change of cocycle representative.

The localization maps and their relation to the augmented dual Selmer kernel are supplied by ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.6 (and D8 in the arbitrary-rank application). No vanishing is assumed merely from a residual-image label.

Splitting in F(ζ_{p^N}) and ordered residual eigenvalues require compatible finite-quotient data. Excluding ramified places of any auxiliary field is part of B; degree one alone does not imply unramified splitting in that field.

The Chebotarev dependency is the explicit open request naming this node in neededBy, following the packet’s existing upstream-request representation. It is a planned theorem, never a pinned library declaration.
proofSteps: Apply the imported Chebotarev Layer 10 theorem to each specified nonempty conjugacy class. Its positive Dirichlet density survives deleting any finite exceptional or avoidance set; this uses the upstream Frobenius-prime-set carrier, not a redefinition of arithmetic Frobenius.

For a number field F, primes of residue degree at least two over Q have a bounded prime sum as s tends to 1 from above: over each rational prime there are at most [F:Q] primes, and their contributions are bounded by [F:Q] times the sum of rational-prime norms to the power −2s. They therefore have Dirichlet density zero. Removing them leaves the positive-density detecting class infinite. This elementary degree-one refinement is part of this application, not an assertion that Layer 10 already exports it.

Start with the kernel H. If it is nonzero, choose a nonzero x in the current kernel and a detecting prime outside all previous choices and B. Intersecting with ker loc_v strictly lowers its finite dimension. Iterate at most dim_k H times. The cohomological supplier identifies the final kernel with the augmented dual Selmer group in each application.

Use the admissible padding class to enlarge the chosen set to exactly q, excluding B and all previous primes at every step. Additional localization conditions preserve injectivity. For H = 0 and q = 0 return the empty set; q > 0 still requires the padding hypothesis.
acceptance: A two-dimensional H with coordinate detecting maps needs two independent detections: detecting only the first coordinate leaves a nonzero kernel. Repeating one prime cannot satisfy the cardinality assertion.
H = 0 admits the empty set for q = 0; an empty admissible set cannot supply q > 0. This tests the non-vacuous padding hypothesis.

Adding finitely many forbidden places, including places over the discriminant of F₀/Q, preserves the construction. Degree-one primes above rational primes ramified in F₀ must still be excluded. For F₀ = Q(i), the place over 2 has residue degree one but 2 ramifies; this is the excluded case.
The ordinary and enormous-image applications verify different detecting-element hypotheses. This lemma cannot turn adequacy into either big or enormous image.

sourceIssues.printed: We say that G satisﬁes the condition Φp if for all ﬁnite index subgroups G′ ⊂ G the maximal pro-p quotient of G′ is topologically ﬁnitely generated. This is equivalent to asking that Hom(G, Fp) is ﬁnite dimensional.
sourceIssues.correction: “This is equivalent to asking that Hom(G′, 𝔽_p) is finite dimensional for every open G′ ⊂ G” (as the same notes' Exercise 1 states).
sourceIssues.reason: Finiteness of Hom(G, 𝔽_p) for G alone is strictly weaker: for p odd, G = (∏_ℕ ℤ/p) ⋊ ℤ/2 with ℤ/2 acting by inversion has abelianisation ℤ/2 (the commutators a^{-2} fill ∏ ℤ/p since 2 is invertible), so Hom(G, 𝔽_p) = 0, while its open subgroup ∏_ℕ ℤ/p of index 2 has infinite Hom to 𝔽_p and is not topologically finitely generated. Exercise 1 on p. 4 of the same notes states the correct equivalence with all open subgroups.
searched: Kisin's Harvard notes page (people.math.harvard.edu/~kisin/notes/), fetched 2026-09-28: a single 4-page PDF, no revision or errata listed.

review.reason: Confirmed at Kisin, Lecture 1, (1.2), p. 1: the printed sentence says Hom(G, Fp) for G itself, while Φ_p quantifies over all finite-index subgroups; the counterexample (∏_ℕ ℤ/p) ⋊ ℤ/2 (p odd) is correct, since the commutators a^{−2} generate ∏ℤ/p, so Hom(G, 𝔽_p) = 0 while the index-2 subgroup has infinite Hom to 𝔽_p. Exercise 1 on p. 4 states the correct equivalence.

sourceIssues.printed: The converse is also true, as one sees easily using the surjectivity of SpC(A) → SpB(A) for A = F[ϵ] ([45]).
sourceIssues.correction: “… using the injectivity of Sp_C(A) → Sp_B(A) for A = 𝔽[ε]”: injectivity on tangent spaces makes the cotangent map surjective, and complete Nakayama then makes B → C surjective.
sourceIssues.reason: The converse assumes that Sp_C(A) → Sp_B(A) is injective for all A; surjectivity of this map is neither given nor true for a proper closed immersion (for B = 𝒪⟦x⟧ → C = 𝒪, the tangent map t_C = 0 → t_B = 𝔽 is not surjective). The argument that works uses injectivity at A = 𝔽[ε].
